question: Under which article of the Constitution is the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India appointed?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 148**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 148** of the Indian Constitution provides for the establishment and appointment of the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India.
 
• The CAG is responsible for auditing the accounts of the Union and State governments and public sector organizations.
 
• The CAG is appointed by the President of India and holds office for a term of six years or until the age of 65, whichever is earlier.
 
• The CAG is an independent authority and is considered the guardian of the public purse.
 
• As per the Constitution, the reports of the CAG are submitted to the President or Governor, who then places them before the legislature for discussion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 324**

 
 
• This article pertains to the establishment and powers of the Election Commission of India.
 
• The Election Commission is responsible for conducting free and fair elections in India for the Parliament, State Legislatures, and the offices of the President and Vice-President.
 
• The Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners are appointed by the President of India.
 
 
 
• **Article 280**
 
 
• This article deals with the formation of the Finance Commission of India.
 
• The Finance Commission is constituted by the President every five years to recommend the distribution of financial resources between the Union and the States.
 
• The recommendations made by the Finance Commission are advisory in nature.
 
 
 
• **Article 76**
 
 
• This article establishes the office of the Attorney General of India.
 
• The Attorney General is the highest legal officer in the country and acts as the chief legal advisor to the Government of India.
 
• The Attorney General is appointed by the President and holds office during their pleasure.
